hints: Notice both loudspeakers are driven by the same signal generator, so they emit sound of the same frequency and with constant phase difference.
Think about the two different distances from the upper and lower loudspeaker to the student's ear and how their difference changes on the walk from P to Q.
Link loud positions to in-phase arrival and quiet positions to antiphase arrival of the two waves, which is the condition for two-source superposition.
walkthrough: The two loudspeakers act as two coherent sources because they are connected to the same signal generator, so they have the same frequency $f$ and wavelength $\lambda$ and a fixed phase relationship.
At any point between P and Q the ear receives one wave from each speaker, and the resultant displacement is the vector sum of the two displacements by the principle of superposition.
As the student moves, the distance to each speaker changes differently, so the path difference $\Delta x$ between the two waves changes continuously.

When $\Delta x = n\lambda$ the waves arrive in phase and add to give large amplitude and loud sound, and when $\Delta x = (n+1/2)\lambda$ they arrive in antiphase and cancel to give small amplitude and quiet sound.
Moving from P to Q passes alternately through in-phase and antiphase conditions, so loudness rises and falls repeatedly due to interference of the sound waves. This is option C.

options.A: Diffraction is spreading of waves around obstacles, but it does not produce repeated loud and quiet positions as the student moves from P to Q.
options.B: Doppler shift changes observed frequency when there is relative motion of source and observer, but walking slowly does not cause repeated rises and falls in loudness.
options.C: The two coherent sound waves superpose, giving constructive interference where loud and destructive interference where quiet as path difference changes.
options.D: Reflection from walls could form echoes, but the regular pattern of maxima and minima between P and Q is due to the two direct waves overlapping.
